title: Explore Everest Base Camp in 7 Stories

slides.caption: Everest Base Camp sits at about 5,364 meters in the Khumbu region.
Most trekkers fly from Kathmandu to Lukla to begin the trek.
Namche Bazaar is the Sherpa capital and a key acclimatization stop.
Tengboche Monastery offers views of Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam.
Yaks carry gear along the high-altitude trails.
Gorak Shep is the last settlement before Base Camp.
Standing at Base Camp is a moment you will never forget.
Chitwan National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Terai plains.
Jeep and walking safaris take you through grassland and jungle.
Spot one-horned rhinoceros, deer, crocodiles and hundreds of bird species.
Experience Tharu culture, dance and local food in nearby villages.
The best time to visit is October to March.
Boudhanath is one of the largest stupas in the world.
Prayer flags and butter lamps fill the square around it.
Walk clockwise around the stupa, as pilgrims have done for centuries.
The painted eyes of the Buddha watch over Kathmandu.
Early mornings in the mountains are cold, quiet and unforgettable.
Poon Hill, Kalapatthar and Nagarkot are classic sunrise viewpoints.
First light turns the snow peaks gold and pink.
Carry a warm jacket and a headlamp for the climb.
Your guide will wake you in time for the best light.
Breakfast always tastes better with a view.
Join us and see the Himalayas wake up.
